# seqera/cyp-substrate-predictor

## Summary

Predicts whether small molecules are **CYP2D6 substrates** from their SMILES
strings. Takes a CSV or SMILES list, emits a CSV of probabilities.

CPU-only, no GPU, no model download — the weights (371 KB) are bundled in the
container. A batch of a few thousand molecules scores in seconds.

## Get started

```nextflow
include { CYPSUBSTRATEPREDICTOR } from 'seqera/cyp-substrate-predictor'

workflow {
    ch_molecules = Channel.of([[id: 'library'], file('molecules.csv')])

    // Second input is an optional weights override; [] uses the bundled model.
    CYPSUBSTRATEPREDICTOR(ch_molecules, [])

    CYPSUBSTRATEPREDICTOR.out.predictions.view()
}
```

## Input

| Input | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `meta` | map | e.g. `[ id:'library' ]` |
| `smiles` | file | CSV with a header naming a SMILES column, or a plain one-per-line list |
| `pretrained_model` | file | Optional weights `.npz`. Pass `[]` for the bundled CYP2D6 model. |

The SMILES column is auto-detected from `smiles`, `canonical_smiles`, `Drug`, or
`structure` (case-insensitive); an `id`/`name`/`compound_id` column is carried
through to the output. TDC benchmark exports work unmodified. A file whose first
line is not a recognised header is read as a bare SMILES list, so `.smi` files do
not lose their first molecule.

## Output

| Output | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `predictions` | file | CSV: `id,smiles,p_substrate,prediction,valid` |
| `versions_cypsubstratepredictor` | topic | version on the `versions` topic |

```csv
id,smiles,p_substrate,prediction,valid
codeine,COc1ccc2C[C@H]3N(C)CC[C@@]45[C@@H](Oc1c24)[C@H](O)C=C[C@H]35,0.9592,1,true
ibuprofen,CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O,0.0613,0,true
unparsable,not_a_smiles,,,false
```

Molecules RDKit cannot parse get `valid=false` and are **left unscored** rather
than given the score of an all-zero feature vector (~0.23), which would look like
a real prediction.

## Configuration

Arguments go through `ext.args`:

```nextflow
process {
    withName: CYPSUBSTRATEPREDICTOR {
        ext.args = '--threshold 0.355'
    }
}
```

`--threshold` sets the probability at which `prediction` flips to 1. The default
is 0.5; **0.355** maximises F1 in cross-validation on the training split and is
usually the better choice for screening — at 0.5 recall is only 0.465.

### Batch, do not fan out

Scoring is a 200×827 matmul per molecule — thousands per second. Run **one task
per file**, not one per molecule, or Nextflow's per-task overhead will dominate
the runtime by orders of magnitude. For very large libraries, chunk upstream:

```nextflow
Channel.fromPath('library.csv')
    .splitCsv(header: true, by: 50_000)
    ...
```

## Performance and limitations

On the held-out TDC test split (135 molecules): **AUPRC 0.779, AUROC 0.858**,
against a random-guess AUPRC of 0.319.

Read [the model card][card] before acting on the output. In short:

- **Trained on 532 molecules, CYP2D6 only.** Says nothing about other CYP
  isoforms, and nothing about *inhibition* — substrate and inhibitor are
  different questions.
- **0.78 is split-specific.** Random 5-fold CV on the training split gives AUPRC
  0.536. Expect behaviour nearer that figure on genuinely novel chemotypes.
- **The benchmark has label noise.** CarbonMangels labels acetaminophen and
  caffeine as CYP2D6 substrates, which standard pharmacology does not support.
- **Out-of-domain input** (peptides, inorganics, very large or polar molecules)
  gets a confident-looking score with nothing behind it.

[card]: https://github.com/seqeralabs/cyp-substrate-predictor/blob/main/docs/model-card.md

## Dependencies

`cyp-substrate-predictor` (Python; rdkit, scikit-learn, numpy, pandas), declared
in `environment.yml`. Requires ~1 CPU and a few hundred MB of memory.

## nf-core compatibility

This module is built to the Nextflow registry spec, but every nf-core-required
file is present (`main.nf`, `meta.yml`, `environment.yml`, `tests/main.nf.test`,
`tests/main.nf.test.snap`) and `main.nf` already follows nf-core conventions:
`process_single` label, `conda`/`container` directives, `task.ext.args` and
`task.ext.prefix`, a `when:` guard, a `stub:` block, and versions emitted via
`eval` on the `versions` topic.

Four mechanical changes would be needed to open an nf-core PR:

1. Rename the directory to `cypsubstratepredictor` — nf-core paths carry no hyphens.
2. In `meta.yml`, drop the `$schema`, `version` and `license` keys and change
   `name` from `seqera/cyp-substrate-predictor` to a bare `cypsubstratepredictor`.
3. Restyle the `input`/`output` entries from the registry's `- name: x` form to
   nf-core's `- x:` mapping form. The registry schema carries the same
   information — including `tools`, `keywords`, `topics` and `ontologies` — so
   this is a reshape, not a rewrite.
4. Move `tests/molecules.csv` into the `modules` branch of
   [nf-core/test-datasets][td] and reference it through
   `params.modules_testdata_base_path`. nf-core does not accept module-local
   fixtures.

Worth knowing before attempting it: nf-core/modules has ~919 modules and
essentially no small-molecule cheminformatics, so a CYP2D6 substrate predictor
would be opening a new domain there. The stronger case pairs it with
[`pharmcat`][pc] — that module derives a patient's CYP2D6 metabolizer status from
genotype, this one scores whether a drug is a CYP2D6 substrate, and together they
make a drug-gene interaction screen.

[td]: https://github.com/nf-core/test-datasets/tree/modules
[pc]: https://nf-co.re/modules/pharmcat

Apache-2.0

---
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/modules/master/modules/environment-schema.json
channels:
  - conda-forge
  - bioconda
dependencies:
  - conda-forge::python=3.12
  - pip:
      - cyp-substrate-predictor==0.2.0

process CYPSUBSTRATEPREDICTOR {
    tag "${meta.id}"
    label 'process_single'

    conda "${moduleDir}/environment.yml"
    container "${ workflow.containerEngine in ['singularity', 'apptainer'] && !task.ext.singularity_pull_docker_container ?
        'oras://community.wave.seqera.io/library/python_cyp-substrate-predictor:11b70b2bd06a4623' :
        'community.wave.seqera.io/library/python_cyp-substrate-predictor:32bfee9c00e01ca7' }"

    input:
    tuple val(meta), path(smiles)
    path(pretrained_model)

    output:
    tuple val(meta), path("${prefix}.csv"), emit: predictions
    tuple val("${task.process}"), val('cyp-substrate-predictor'), eval("cyp-substrate-predict --version"), topic: versions, emit: versions_cypsubstratepredictor

    when:
    task.ext.when == null || task.ext.when

    script:
    def args = task.ext.args ?: ''
    def model_command = pretrained_model ? "--pretrained-model ${pretrained_model}" : ''
    prefix = task.ext.prefix ?: "${meta.id}"
    """
    cyp-substrate-predict \\
        --input ${smiles} \\
        --output ${prefix}.csv \\
        ${model_command} \\
        ${args}
    """

    stub:
    prefix = task.ext.prefix ?: "${meta.id}"
    """
    echo "id,smiles,p_substrate,prediction,valid" > ${prefix}.csv
    """
}

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nextflow-io/schemas/refs/heads/main/module/v1/schema.json
$schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nextflow-io/schemas/refs/heads/main/module/v1/schema.json
name: seqera/cyp-substrate-predictor
version: 0.2.0
description: Predict whether small molecules are CYP2D6 substrates from their SMILES
license: Apache-2.0
keywords:
  - cheminformatics
  - admet
  - cytochrome-p450
  - cyp2d6
  - drug-metabolism
  - smiles
  - machine-learning
tools:
  - cyp-substrate-predictor:
      description: >
        CPU-only interpretable classifier for CYP2D6 substrate prediction. Pairs
        count-Morgan fingerprints with the Extended Reduced Graph (ErG)
        pharmacophore descriptor and a random-subspace bagged logistic
        regression. AUPRC 0.779 on the held-out TDC ADMET test split; the 371 KB
        of weights are bundled, so nothing is downloaded at runtime.
      homepage: https://github.com/seqeralabs/cyp-substrate-predictor
      documentation: https://github.com/seqeralabs/cyp-substrate-predictor/blob/main/docs/model-card.md
      tool_dev_url: https://github.com/seqeralabs/cyp-substrate-predictor
      licence: ["Apache-2.0"]
      identifier: ""
input:
  - - name: meta
      type: map
      description: |
        Groovy Map containing batch information, e.g. [ id:'library1' ]
    - name: smiles
      type: file
      description: >
        Molecules to score. Either a CSV whose header names a SMILES column
        (smiles, canonical_smiles, Drug or structure, case-insensitive) and
        optionally an id column, or a plain one-SMILES-per-line list. Identifiers
        are carried through to the output.
      pattern: "*.{csv,tsv,smi,txt}"
      ontologies:
        - edam: http://edamontology.org/format_1196 # SMILES
        - edam: http://edamontology.org/format_3752 # CSV
  - name: pretrained_model
    type: file
    description: >
      Optional weights .npz to use in place of the CYP2D6 model bundled in the
      container, for example a model retrained for another isoform. Pass [] (an
      empty list) to use the bundled default.
    pattern: "*.npz"
    ontologies: []
output:
  - - name: meta
      type: map
      description: |
        Groovy Map containing batch information, e.g. [ id:'library1' ]
    - name: predictions
      type: file
      description: >
        CSV with columns id, smiles, p_substrate, prediction, valid. p_substrate
        is P(CYP2D6 substrate); prediction applies --threshold (default 0.5).
        SMILES that RDKit cannot parse have valid=false and are left unscored
        rather than given the score of an all-zero feature vector.
      pattern: "*.csv"
      ontologies:
        - edam: http://edamontology.org/format_3752 # CSV
  - - name: task_process
      type: string
      description: Name of the process emitting the version
    - name: tool
      type: string
      description: Name of the tool
    - name: version
      type: string
      description: Version of cyp-substrate-predictor
topics:
  - - name: task_process
      type: string
      description: Name of the process emitting the version
    - name: tool
      type: string
      description: Name of the tool
    - name: version
      type: string
      description: Version of cyp-substrate-predictor
authors:
  - "@evanfloden"
maintainers:
  - "@evanfloden"
